title: First post… just wanted to show off some progress
author: ItsmeMartyBee
selftext:
I’m making a game called **Berry and Malli**, and one of the biggest parts of the project for me has been figuring out how to use AI as a **production tool**, rather than having AI make the game for me.  
I’m doing the actual design work—gameplay systems, world design, mechanics, art direction, balance, etc.—and using tools like Codex to help me build the pipeline I need to create it. For example, I bought modular environment assets, then used AI to help me build a terrain-construction tool around them. When I needed roads, I had it help me make a road painter. When I run into repetitive production problems, I try to build a tool that lets *me* solve them faster.  
The game itself is a foraging/action RPG inspired by my wife and my dog. Malli is a wolfkin who can sniff out materials and distinguish safe herbs and mushrooms from poisonous lookalikes. In sniff mode, the right stick controls Berry so she can gather what he finds. Berry can forage by herself too, but she can’t always tell the difference between safe and poisonous ingredients.  
Berry is the inventor of the pair. She turns what you forage into traps, constructs, harvesting tools, potions, elixirs, and brews. In the clip, she makes a **Feral Brew**, which temporarily heightens her senses enough to smell almost as well as Malli.  
My hope is to eventually make the game profitable and use part of what it earns to support **animal welfare**.  
I’d genuinely love feedback—especially from people experimenting with AI-assisted game development or workflows where AI helps build the tools while the developer remains in control of the creative decisions. :)

**TL;DR:** I’m building *Berry and Malli* myself, while using AI primarily to create coding and production tools that help me implement my ideas faster—not to generate the game for me. The goal is a fun foraging/action RPG that can hopefully also help support animal welfare.

replies.author: ItsmeMartyBee
replies.body: Thanks! Been working on it for like… 4 months so far

comments.author: DjPersh
comments.body: Looks cool! Mind derailing a bit about how you created to models an animations?

replies.author: ItsmeMartyBee
replies.body: I bought an asset pack called kaykit, bought the source assets for a really affordable price. Kaykit had a lot of animations, built in to their rigs. So at first I was kit bashing some of the models together but didn’t get the look I wanted, so I remodeled some of the assets in blender.  Basically tweaked the proportions and painted them. I used ChatGPT to guide me through the process, so I also got a little crash course in blender too

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body:
I love your goal to use the profits of the game to support a charity / social cause! Well done on the experience and I think it's a very good idea to use free models from Kaykit.

Games as social awareness tools is awesome, this reminds me of PETA's (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals) [parody and original games ](https://www.peta.org/features/games/)from the 2010s where they used the games to promote their cause.

Or maybe you've played [The McDonald's Video game](https://www.molleindustria.org/mcdonalds/) from [Molleindustria](https://www.molleindustria.org/) who is a Carnegie Mellon professor who has built many video games / video game adjacent experiences to raise awareness for social issues?

How do you plan on adding the financial transaction part of the game? What will the in app purchase surfaces look like? How will you promote this? Asking because I'm also interested in making a game with the express goal of raising money to turn the experience of in app transactions into something more philanthropic - kind of like the social validation and fun of the ALS ice bucket challenge + YouTube but for games

replies.author: ItsmeMartyBee
replies.body: I haven’t thought that far ahead yet as I’m still in the design phase, but what I was thinking was simultaneously offering this game for 10 dollars and then donating 10% directly to the humane society of America as they help with not only pets but also live stock and animals tested. I was also thinking of looking into implementing a way to send download codes to people who upload a screenshot of a direct donation to them for the same amount
